Generally, there are two justifications for perceived benefits from note taking: the encoding function and the external storage function. The encoding function posits that the process of taking notes facilitates learning, whereas the external storage function suggests that notes serve as a record to be reviewed later. The present study examined the effects of note-taking method (longhand vs. laptop) and note review (review vs. no review) on test performance. Undergraduate participants (N = 120) viewed a video lecture and took notes either longhand or on a laptop, then either reviewed their notes for 10 minutes or engaged in a distractor task.
